title: Ptychography scan positions ignore the calibrated R–Q rotation and transpose
evidence: Closed 2026-09-09 through Gate D with an independent refuter (docs/archive/closed-items-2026-09.md:533-545; docs/archive/2026-09-09-review/d002-d003-gate-d.md). At HEAD the positions are rotated about their mean by calibration.rotationRad and swapped on calibration.transpose (PtychographyPreparation.swift:184-200), with the axis mapping and the padding DEVIATION documented at :115-170.

title: H5Reader's three attribute readers read the whole attribute into a fixed-size scalar buffer — a multi-element HDF5 attribute overruns it
evidence: Closed 2026-09-09 (docs/archive/closed-items-2026-09.md:533-545). attributeIsScalar (H5Reader.swift:893-898) checks H5Aget_space element count == 1 and all three attribute readers call it (:982, :998, :1041). The same missing guard remains in the sidecar reader (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:2313, no h5agetSpace), which docs/open-items.md:282-286 tracks.

title: Learned detector: the edge-exclusion rule is applied to each 256 px model window, so on detectors > 256 px there are blind bands at every window seam where no window will accept a peak
evidence: Each 256-px window's peaks go through DiskDetector.refine with a 256x256 detector (LearnedDiskDetector.swift:428-431), and refine rejects anything within edgeBoundary of the WINDOW edge (DiskDetection.swift:803). The seams are blind wherever the real window overlap is less than 2*edgeBoundary. Worked case: on a 1024-px detector the defaults give edgeBoundary 42 (DiskDetection.swift:417) and windows at 0/192/384/576/768 (:232-243, overlap 64), leaving ~20 px bands per seam per axis (e.g. global x 214-233) where no window accepts a peak. 512 px is unaffected (overlap 128); 480 px gets 8 px bands.

title: A multi-`data_` CIF is silently merged into one crystal: cell parameters from the last block, atom sites and symmetry operations concatenated from all of them
evidence: parse() keeps only the first data_ name (CIFImport.swift:200-206). It never resets state at a new block: scalar tags overwrite cellValues so the last block's cell wins (:262-266), and atom-site and symop loops are appended across blocks (:246-255). It is not a repeat of core-crystal-02, which was the missing-symops refusal (:356-365). CrystalModel's 0.5 Å close-contact validation will reject some merged files, but not ones whose extra atoms land farther apart.

title: The shipped detector's public record claims 20 000 training steps; the retained training log shows the 90-minute cap fired at step 6 500
evidence: The record says "steps": 20000 (json:12). The repo's own run note says the 90-minute train ran 6 500 steps (docs/archive/v3/learned-detector-2026-09-06.md:574). 20000 is train.py's --steps default (tools/disk-detector/train.py:126), and the LR schedule is sized to it (:150). So the record gives the configured budget, not the executed count. This is a provenance and doc fix only.

title: The triage's own port recipe for DiffractionEmbedding omits its build prerequisite, which exists only on the branch
evidence: Superseded: the C8 'stay on branch' decision was reversed 09-11 (docs/decisions.md:62) and the port happened. mac4DSTEM/Core/Analysis/DiffractionEmbedding.swift and mac4DSTEMTests/DiffractionEmbeddingTests.swift are on main and wired (App/AppState+DiffractionGroups.swift). The triage doc is archive-only, so a missing prerequisite in its recipe no longer affects anything.

title: The C8 decision to strand the four pure engines rests on a claim the branch's own files and gate rows contradict
evidence: Superseded: docs/decisions.md:62 records '09-08 C8 engines stay on branch (reversed 09-11)'. The engines are on main: Core/Analysis/Precipitates/{PrecipitateReflections,PrecipitateSegmentation,PrecipitateStatistics}.swift and Core/Analysis/DiffractionEmbedding.swift.

title: The accessibility crash — the one finding status.md names as able to block v3.0.0 — rests on two crash reports that do not exist on this machine
evidence: Moot at HEAD: the accessibility crash no longer blocks a release (owner decision 2026-09-11, docs/open-items.md:527), and the entry now says the two crash reports' evidence 'aged off 2026-09-15' (:532-533). Whether they existed on the owner's machine on 09-09 cannot be checked from the repo. Only a new reproduction under an AX client would settle it.

title: A file- or sidecar-supplied probe radius permanently freezes `minPeakSpacing`: the later measured radius is never adopted, because the "user has not chosen one" guard cannot tell an app-seeded value from a user edit
evidence: At load, minPeakSpacing is seeded from the file's probe radius via fittedProbeRadius (AppState+Open.swift:622-624, DiskDetection.swift:403-414). refreshForMeasuredProbe only updates it when the value still equals the probeRadius:nil placeholder (DiskDetectionProduct.swift:90-99). Example: a file-supplied r=6 on a 256 detector seeds spacing 6, not the placeholder 32, so a later measured r=9 is never adopted. The guard cannot tell app-seeded from user-set.

title: A replayed DPC step reports `.published` while publishing nothing — the promote run's summary attests to a result that was never produced
evidence: True: applyDPCDisplay publishes only when navigation.analysisMode == .dpc and otherwise returns nil as 'success' (AppState+DPC.swift:119). runDPC then writes 'DPC ✓', records the step and returns .published (:59-73). The replay DPC case never sets the mode (AppState+Replay.swift:155-169), and after a promote the mode is the restored one (AppState+Open.swift:645-646). A promote from any other mode therefore reports a DPC step with no product. Wrong part: the CoM field itself IS computed and stored (comField, :51), so 'never produced' overstates it.

title: `publishProduct` takes the product's pixel size from the CURRENT analysis mode, so the scan-domain detector-disagreement map is published and exported with the Bragg map's reciprocal Å⁻¹/px
evidence: runDiskDisagreement publishes a domain:.scan map from the Disks mode (AppState+DiskDetection.swift:414-420). publishProduct takes its sampling from currentScalarPersistenceMetadata (AppState.swift:371, 381), which in .disks returns qPixelSize/qPixelUnits (Support/ResultExport.swift:1445-1453). The product's extraProvenance overrides coordinate_space to 'real' (Core/ML/LearnedDiskDetection.swift:64) but not the sampling. The test pins domain only (mac4DSTEMTests/LearnedDetectionSessionTests.swift:165-170). Not a repeat of core-data-02 (session-restore shape check).

title: Disk-detection staleness signature and recipe omit the probe kernel's identity, so a Bragg map made with a different kernel is reported as current
evidence: The staleness signature is diskParams.replayParameters(kernel:) (App/ProductWorkflow.swift:459-460), which carries only kernel_source, kernel_mode and kernel_probe_path (DiskDetection.swift:527-529). It omits the radius and trench that provenance records (:495-497). Regenerating a synthetic kernel after a new origin fit, or a measured kernel from a different ROI, replaces probeKernel (AppState+DiskDetection.swift:49, 77, 122, 148) without changing the signature or invalidating the Bragg vectors.

title: A single non-finite pixel in a diffraction pattern silently returns zero peaks for that whole pattern
evidence: Nothing in the disk-detection path or the readers filters non-finite pixels. One NaN/Inf pixel makes every FFT bin NaN (DiskDetection.swift:847), so the thresholded correlation is NaN or 0 everywhere (:868). The strict 8-neighbour tests at :899 then find no maximum, and the pattern returns 0 peaks with no flag. py4DSTEM would also propagate NaN. Whether real files carry NaN pixels is not established.

title: Hexagonal IPF colour key labels ⟨10-1̄0⟩ and ⟨11-2̄0⟩ the wrong way round — green and blue are swapped against the crystallography
evidence: ipfColor puts green at azimuth 0 and blue at 30° (OrientationResult.swift:474-479). The direction is the zone axis in the crystal Cartesian frame (:696; the plan's g vectors are Cartesian in latReal, Crystal.swift:103-106, with x ∥ a1). a1 is the ⟨11-20⟩ family and 30° is ⟨10-10⟩ (2a1+a2 lies at 30°). Yet the docstring (:468) and the legend (UI/PaneOverlays.swift:1045, 1049, 1054) call (1,0,0) '10-10'. So the labels are swapped against the code's own frame. docs/open-items.md:171-174 lists this as 'may be' and says it must be settled first.

title: Float32 running sum saturates: whole-stack mean collapses on ordinary-sized datasets
evidence: stack.reduce(0, +) on [Float] accumulates in Float32 and only converts to Double afterwards (ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:422). The stack values are normalized to about 1 with 1.0 padding (:369, :414-415), so the running sum stops growing near 2^25 (≈33.5M). Stacks are allowed up to ~134M elements (1 GiB resident, :127, :356-361). Example: a 256x256 scan with 32 px padding and ~700 BF pixels (58M elements) gives stackMean ≈0.57 instead of ≈1. The same pattern appears at ParallaxAlignment.swift:445. py4DSTEM uses numpy's pairwise mean.

title: Empty scan positions inject Float.greatestFiniteMagnitude into the clustering-scale median
evidence: nearest starts at Float.greatestFiniteMagnitude, and the guard `if nearest.isFinite` is always true for that value. So every position with no peak beyond minRadius appends 3.4e38 (StrainMapping.swift:383-388). Below 50% empty positions this pushes the median (and clusterTolerance, :390-391) upward. Above 50% the tolerance becomes ~6e37, everything merges into one cluster, and basis estimation fails.

title: Every full-cube VirtualDetector pass runs on the main actor: AppState never wraps them in Task.detached, and `nonisolated async` inherits the caller's actor under this project's settings
evidence: VirtualDetector is a nonisolated enum and its tiled* entry points are plain async (VirtualDetector.swift:252-279). Both the package (Package.swift enables NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault) and the app (project.pbxproj SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY=YES) run such functions on the caller's actor. AppState calls them directly, not via Task.detached (AppState+ResultPresentation.swift:57, 147, 252-275; AppState+Calibration.swift:30, 292), so the synchronous Metal waits (:306-312) run on the main actor. The file header (:13-15) claims otherwise. docs/open-items.md:235-240 records the same mechanism freezing the Friedel pass.

title: Selected-area diffraction circle mask is half a pixel off-centre from the ROI drawn on screen
evidence: The circle region is centred at (scanX+0.5, scanY+0.5) (VirtualDetector.swift:92-94), but makeMask measures from integer pixel indices (:600-611, dx = Float(x) - cx). That puts the mask centre on the corner between pixels, half a pixel down-right. The on-screen ROI is centred on the selected pixel's centre ((x+0.5)*scale in edge coordinates, UI/ImagePanes.swift:1143-1144). Example: radius 1 gives a 2x2 block at x..x+1, y..y+1 instead of a symmetric cross.

title: CIF importer applies whatever symmetry-operation list the file happens to contain, with no completeness or consistency check
evidence: The listed operators are applied as-is whenever any is non-identity (CIFImport.swift:343-351). There is no check of group closure, of the count against the declared space group, or of centring. The only symop checks are syntax checks (:569-640). Mitigation: CrystalModel's 0.5 Å close-contact validation rejects some inconsistent results. The trigger is a malformed or hand-edited CIF.

title: ACOM CPU matching silently returns an unmatched or partially unmatched orientation map when a per-worker matcher cannot be built — no failure flag, unlike its DiskDetection twin
evidence: In the CPU path, a worker whose OrientationMatcher init fails just returns (OrientationMatcher.swift:683-685). Its positions keep their default result and the map is returned as success (:715). The only failure in init is FFT1D(n: nAzimuthal) (:107-108), which depends on the plan, so in practice it fails for every worker or none. That gives an all-unmatched map, not a silent partial one. Plausibility is low.

title: Exported dim vectors pair a defaulted step of 1 with a real physical unit, manufacturing a calibration that was never measured
evidence: Step and unit fall back independently: rSize ?? 1 with rUnits ?? "pixels" (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1316-1330), and pixelSizeRow ?? rSize ?? 1 with pixelUnits ?? rUnits (:1835-1841). Units can be set with no size: setManualRPixelUnits sets units without a size (App/AppState+Open.swift:1159-1166), and clearing a manual size keeps the units (:1149-1157). Either way the export writes dim [0, 1] labelled e.g. 'nm'.

title: A session save silently publishes a stripped sidecar when the existing file cannot be opened, destroying BraggVectors, saved results, the replay record and the labels
evidence: When the sidecar exists but H5Fopen fails, existingID is quietly nil (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1423-1428). A missing root group is also tolerated (:1449-1452). The rewrite then carries forward no results, replay record, labels or braggvectors (:1448-1498), and the temp file is atomically renamed over the original (:1082-1085). One plausible trigger: another process holds the sidecar open for writing (HDF5 file lock).

title: `hasEllipse` admits a non-positive semi-axis, so a degenerate ellipse is applied to every Bragg vector while readiness reports "No detector-distortion correction"
evidence: hasEllipse only requires finite values and a != 0 (Calibration.swift:852-855), so b <= 0 or a < 0 passes. ellipseTransform then applies e = b/a (:884-893) to every offset. Readiness separately requires a > 0 and b > 0 and shows 'No detector-distortion correction' (:327-338). An imported a=1, b=0 collapses one axis with the UI saying no correction applies. Such input is unlikely from py4DSTEM.

title: DM4 parsing has unguarded trapping Int conversions and an unbounded field loop — a corrupt or desynchronised tag tree kills or hangs the process
evidence: Int(UInt64) traps on values >= 2^63 at DM4Reader.swift:473 and at :501, which runs before the ninfo guard at :503. The same trap exists at :518, 527, 531 and 540. `for f in 0..<nFields` is bounded only by the tag value (:520, :532), so a garbage count like 2^40 hangs the process. 4+nFields*2 and length*elemSize (:537, :541) can overflow-trap. Int(Double) on tag values traps on NaN or out-of-range (:673, :744). Well-formed files are fine; it takes a corrupt or desynchronised tag tree.

title: Scan-fastest DM4 reads the detector pair in the opposite order from the detector-fastest branch, and the only test covering it is circular
evidence: Confirmed in code: the detector-fastest branch maps the fastest detector tag to Qx (shape [dims3,dims2,dims1,dims0]). The scan-fastest branch maps the faster detector tag to Qy (shape [dims1,dims0,dims2,dims3]; DM4Reader.swift:592-599, strides :164-166). The repo's own detail note says the fixture was generated from the code's model (docs/archive/v3/open-items-detail-2026-09-16.md:674-682). Whether the scan-fastest mapping is actually wrong is unsettled. docs/open-items.md:288-293 needs a GMS width read or an ncempy checksum on Si-SiGe.dm4 to decide. It is related to, not a repeat of, core-data-07 (scan-shape dictionary order).

title: The unit gate's end-to-end fixture and every gated `probeSize` fixture are square and centre-symmetric, so an rx/ry or qx/qy swap is undetectable
evidence: True for probeSize: ProbeSizeTests uses q=64 square patterns with disks at (31.5, 31.5) (mac4DSTEMTests/ProbeSizeTests.swift:17, 140-144), so an x0/y0 swap cannot be seen. For the demo cube it overstates: the cube is square (12x12x64x64, DemoFourDDataSource.swift:9), but the pattern is not swap-symmetric. The beam shifts by (-phase, +0.6*phase) with phase ∝ scanX-scanY, and the texture term is asymmetric (:113-142). A qx/qy or rx/ry swap would therefore change the data. Whether any gated assertion would catch it was not checked.

title: A detector smaller than 256 px whose beam is off-centre is silently truncated by the learned frame — part of the detector is never searched
evidence: For an axis shorter than 256, the only window starts at round(probeCentre) - 128 (LearnedDiskDetector.swift:234; fitOffset :189-191). Detector pixels more than 128 px from the beam on that axis fall outside it. Example: qx=240 with the beam at x=60 gives the window [-68, 188), so columns 188-239 are never searched. The crop origin goes only into provenance (:478-479), and no warning is raised.

title: A learned-inference failure on the live overlay is silently answered with CLASSICAL rings while the picker still says Neural net
evidence: livePeaks returns nil for every learned failure: no probe reference, missing asset, a prepare error, or detect returning nil (Session/LearnedDetection.swift:181-193). performLiveDetection treats nil as 'not learned' and falls through to classical detection (AppState+DiskDetection.swift:205-221). The rings drawn are classical, with the funnel diagnostics set, while detectorClass stays .learned.

title: Hand-clicked disk-centre labels are written with `frame: "native"` but are captured in the loaded view's frame, so labels clicked on a cropped or binned view name the wrong detector pixels and scan positions
evidence: toggleDiskCentre stores the click in loaded-view detector pixels (bounded by descriptor.qy/qx) at the loaded-view selectedScan (Support/ResultExport.swift:1266-1287) and applies no crop, bin or scan-origin mapping. encodedJSON always writes frame: "native" (Session/DiskCentreLabels.swift:223-233). The label UI is not disabled on cropped or binned views (UI/MapSettings.swift:366). Not a repeat of support-export-08 (Bragg CSV provenance).

title: ApertureOverlay's accessibility representation builds a Slider whose ClosedRange can be inverted, trapping the process
evidence: The outer-radius accessibility slider range is max(1, inner)...Float(max(W, H)) (PaneOverlays.swift:479-480). That traps whenever inner > max(W, H), or inner is NaN. The drag handlers put no upper bound on outer (:640, :652) and let inner follow outer (:637), so in annulus mode dragging outer and then inner past the detector size reaches it. Replay also accepts any inner <= outer (Session/ReplayPlan.swift:676-677). Whether SwiftUI builds the representation without an AX client was not checked.

title: Pan clamp is still the dead Metal shader's rule, so a zoomed pane can only pan 1/zoom of the way to the image edge
evidence: The clamp is |offset| <= size*(1-1/zoom)/2 (ZoomPan.swift:44-54). The panes apply .scaleEffect(drawZoom) followed by .offset in screen points (UI/ImagePanes.swift:290-291, 826-827). Reaching the image edge needs size*(zoom-1)/2, and the clamp allows exactly 1/zoom of that. At zoom 4 the edge band of each side can't be panned into view (only 3/8 of the needed 3/2 widths).

title: A DPC unit test turns a total DPC failure into a skip, on the always-available in-memory demo fixture
evidence: testDPCDisplayModesPublishTheirOwnProduct (SessionCalibrationTranslationTests.swift:116-124) opens the in-memory demo fixture (AppState+Open.swift:128-133, DemoFourDDataSource, no file) and throws XCTSkip when runDPC leaves no image/RGBA, so a DPC regression that publishes nothing (e.g. runDPC returning .failed from computeCoMField or applyDPCDisplay) reads as a skip, not a failure; the run's AnalysisRunOutcome is discarded (`_ =`).

title: The ACOM Metal-vs-CPU parity gate compares in-plane angles modulo π, so a 180° divergence in the user-selectable "Metal GPU" backend passes while printing "Metal choices exact"
evidence: main.swift:163-178 compares CPU vs Metal inPlaneAngle via truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: .pi) and prints 'PASS: Metal choices exact', so a 180-degree Metal/CPU split passes. On this fixture the plan has no wavelength (main.swift:134-136, OrientationPlan.swift:109 default nil), so templates are pi-periodic and the pi tie is legitimate here (the file says so at :313-318); the real gap is that no gated harness checks Metal vs CPU on a wavelength-built plan (real-acom-benchmark/main.swift:136-140 is also mod pi). Overlaps core-crystal-03.

title: The "AppState never net positive" rule measures two file paths, so AppState growth in any additional `extension AppState` file is invisible — and 630 such lines already exist on ml/disk-detector
evidence: True that the C5 measurement sums only AppState.swift + Support/ResultExport.swift (run-tests.sh:190), while 13 App/AppState+*.swift extension files (4,667 lines) are unmeasured. But the rule no longer blocks (report-only since owner 2026-09-16, run-tests.sh:208-215), Swift extensions cannot add stored properties so new stored state can only land in AppState.swift, and ml/disk-detector no longer exists on origin (git ls-remote shows only main and the cloud branch).

title: `strain-frame-test` generates its golden from whichever py4DSTEM is installed (0.14.17 here) while asserting source-locks against the 0.14.19 pin; its own error text claims a PYTHONPATH that run.sh never sets
evidence: run.sh:20 runs reference.py with no PYTHONPATH, unlike its peers (bragg-export-test/run.sh:31, sidecar-result-test/run.sh:31 set PYTHONPATH=References/py4DSTEM-dev), so reference.py:37-46 imports whatever py4DSTEM the resolved interpreter has installed and its error text ('Run via run.sh, which sets PYTHONPATH') is false; the source locks meanwhile read References/py4DSTEM-dev (reference.py:67-71), so the golden and the locks can come from different versions. The installed version on the owner's machine (0.14.17 claimed) cannot be checked here.

title: `ProbeKernel.synthetic` and the trench in `ProbeKernel.measured` use `y < py/2` for the wrapped (fftfreq) coordinate, where the flat route and NumPy use `(py+1)/2` — one row and one column carry the wrong radius on odd-sized detectors
evidence: synthetic() uses `y < py / 2 ? y : y - py` (ProbeKernel.swift:112,114) and measured()'s trench does the same (:207,209), while the flat route uses `(py + 1) / 2` (:274,276) and py4DSTEM's trench uses mod(arange(N)+N//2, N)-N//2 (probe.py:638-641), which equals fftfreq; for odd N=5 row 2 gets -3 instead of 2. Only odd detector sizes (e.g. an odd crop) are affected, and only one row/column at radius ~N/2, so it changes the kernel only when the trench outer radius (2r) reaches ~N/2.

title: Disk-centre labels written by a branch build are silently erased by any main build, and vice versa — the two designs use different sidecar attribute names
evidence: The competing branch design is gone: ml/disk-detector is absent from origin (git ls-remote lists only main and cloud/2026-09-23-precipitate-objects) and its DiskLabelStore design is recorded as superseded by Session/DiskCentreLabels.swift (docs/archive/git-cleanup-2026-09-17.md:70). main uses one attribute, mac4dstem_disk_centre_labels (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:34), and preserves it across rewrites (:1491-1500, :1642-1644). Only a sidecar written by an old branch build could still lose labels.

title: `ml/disk-detector` is 26 commits BEHIND main as well as 27 ahead; its `tools/` tree would resurrect three harnesses main deleted and a 105-line-stale `sources.manifest`
evidence: ml/disk-detector no longer exists on the remote: git ls-remote --heads origin returns only main (075c044) and cloud/2026-09-23-precipitate-objects. The main-only directive (CLAUDE.md) and docs/archive/git-cleanup-2026-09-17.md:70,90 record the branch's audit and deletion.

title: CONTRIBUTING.md tells public contributors every Core/ change needs a parity fixture; CLAUDE.md explicitly says the opposite, and recent Core/ sessions followed CLAUDE.md
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md no longer says every Core/ change needs a parity fixture: its rules section (CONTRIBUTING.md:61-67) now defers to CLAUDE.md Hard rules (Gate D, Gate B, DEVIATION notes), and grep finds no 'parity fixture' requirement. The clone is shallow, so the commit that changed it cannot be named (last commits touching the file include ee0706c).

title: `Package.swift`'s header says the app target still compiles Core/ and Session/ directly; the project file says it does not, and the 78-path exception list that makes that true is hand-maintained and ungated
evidence: Package.swift:4-7 still says 'The Xcode app target still compiles these same sources directly', while project.pbxproj:59-163 excludes Core/ and Session/ from the app target through a hand-written membershipExceptions list and links DSTEMCore/DSTEMSession (:13-14). No gate checks that list (no reference in tools/run-tests.sh), and it has already drifted: Session/DPCProduct.swift and Session/DiskDetectionProduct.swift are not in it, so the app target also compiles them. Whether that causes a build or behaviour difference needs an Xcode build to settle.

title: Consolidation gate C3 is marked CLOSED but its stated exit criterion fails again on the current status.md, so `/pickup` with no target would re-take a closed gate
evidence: The consolidation plan exited 2026-09-11 and now lives only at docs/archive/consolidation-plan.md (C3 CLOSED at :572). /pickup reads docs/status.md and treats closed consolidation gates as history (.claude/skills/pickup/SKILL.md:12,25-28), so a no-target pickup can no longer take C3.

title: The crash reports that are the sole evidence for the repo's top open item are not on this machine
evidence: The doc now says the evidence is gone: docs/open-items.md:531-533 says 'Two crash reports, evidence aged off 2026-09-15, suspect named', and the item is no longer the top open item (it sits under Accessibility, deferred by owner decision 2026-09-11). Whether the reports exist on any machine cannot be checked from this repo.

title: A promote-and-replay from a detector-cropped or binned rehearsal refuses its own strain/ACOM steps: the executor writes re-referenced disk parameters, the staleness check compares them against the un-re-referenced recipe
evidence: Holds for a BINNED rehearsal: replay writes re-referenced params (AppState+Replay.swift disk step `diskDetection.diskParams = params`; lengths x bin via ReplayPlan.swift:170-175,236-238), a replaying run records nothing (AppState.swift:333) and the recipe keeps rehearsal values (ReplayExecutionTests.swift:291-296). diskDetectionSettingsAreStale (AppState.swift:503-507) therefore compares e.g. sigma_cc 4.0 vs 2.0 and runStrainMapping (AppState.swift:1433) and ACOM (AppState+ACOM.swift:192) refuse. It does not hold for a detector crop at bin 1: disk_detection keys are lengths/invariants only (ReplayPlan.swift:236-240), and a crop leaves lengths unchanged.

title: iDPC integration and the Bragg-vector-map histogram run on the MainActor, the same shape as the P1 freeze this repo already diagnosed one layer up
evidence: applyDPCDisplay runs integrateIDPC/integratePhysicalIDPC (2x zero-padded FFT) synchronously on the MainActor-isolated AppState (AppState+DPC.swift:108,149-165), and showBraggMap calibrates every peak and builds the histogram synchronously (AppState+DiskDetection.swift:384-393). The placement is confirmed; the actual stall (ms vs s on a large scan/peak count) is unmeasured, and a main-thread timing on a large dataset would settle whether it is a user-visible freeze.

title: CIF import runs the whole parse, symmetry expansion and O(n²) family verification synchronously on the main actor, with no cancellation
evidence: importCrystalModel (AppState+Open.swift:104-117) reads and calls CIFImport.crystalModel synchronously on the main actor with no cancellation token; expand() (CIFImport.swift:706-757) is O((sites x ops)^2) via kept.contains (:740). Typical CIFs (tens of sites, <=192 ops) finish quickly, so a visible hang needs an unusually large structure.

title: A signature that cannot be built is reported as "not stale", the same verdict as "matches on every key"
evidence: stalenessVerdict returns .current when currentSignature is nil (ProductWorkflow.swift:394-395), and currentReplaySignature returns nil for disks when no kernel exists and for ACOM with no resolved model (:434-466), so a retained disk/ACOM product whose signature can't be rebuilt reads 'current' in the sidebar/inspector and passes diskDetectionSettingsAreStale (AppState.swift:503-507). The only effect is a missing stale label or guard.

title: DPC colour-wheel traps (hard crash) on a single non-finite centre-of-mass value
evidence: colorWheelRGBA computes hue = atan2(cy,cx) with no finiteness check (DPC.swift:173-181) and hsvToRGB does Int(h6) (:188), which traps on NaN; a NaN value also traps in UInt8(r*255). A pattern containing a +Inf pixel (e.g. gain-normalised data with a dead pixel) gives sumI=Inf and comX=Inf/Inf=NaN in CenterOfMass.metal:57-66. No loader sanitises non-finite pixels, so switching DPC display to Color wheel on such data crashes.

title: Learned-detector runs record min_absolute_intensity, subpixel and upsample_factor in provenance although refine() applies none of them
evidence: The learned path's provenance starts from params.provenance (LearnedDiskDetector.swift:468), which writes subpixel, upsample_factor, min_absolute_intensity and min_relative_intensity (DiskDetection.swift:476-497). Learned refine() (DiskDetection.swift:776-839) always does the parabola and applies no intensity cut (its doc says so), and the replay step records the same keys. The recorded values are false precision but move no peak.

title: Parabolic subpixel refinement runs in Float32 where py4DSTEM explicitly upcasts to float64, with no DEVIATION note
evidence: polyRefine (DiskDetection.swift:988-997) and learned refine (:821-823) evaluate the parabola in Float, while py4DSTEM get_maxima_2D casts the six samples .astype(np.float64) (preprocess/utils.py:218-223), and the three DEVIATION notes in the file (:364, :767, :917) do not cover it. The size of the effect is unmeasured and probably sub-1e-3 px except on near-flat maxima.

title: fit1D reports didNotConverge when the seed is already at (or reaches) the optimum
evidence: The LM loop sets converged only inside the `trial.cost < current.cost` branch when relativeStep < 1e-10 (EllipseCalibration.swift:283-314). At an optimum every trial is rejected (damping x10), so a seed at or reaching the minimum ends in FitError.didNotConverge unless float rounding happens to make a tiny step 'decrease' the cost. The shipped fixtures pass, so how often it fires on real data is unmeasured.

title: Ellipse calibration cannot be cancelled; the cancellation token only discards the finished result
evidence: calibrateEllipse creates a token (AppState+Calibration.swift:177-181) but passes none to EllipseCalibration.fitBestAvailable inside Task.detached (:183-189), and EllipseCalibration.swift has no cancellation checks; the token is read only after the fit returns (:190-193). The fit is one pattern and bounded to 100 LM iterations, so the uncancellable window is short.

title: normalizedResidual carries two incommensurable definitions in one field, gated by near-identical thresholds
evidence: For the conic model, normalizedResidual is sqrt(sum(((conic-1)*I)^2)/sum(I^2)), an intensity-weighted algebraic residual (EllipseCalibration.swift:244-252,323). For the asymmetric-Gaussian model it is RMS(model-data)/dynamicRange (:646). Both go into the same field (:369, :659) with limits of 0.2 (or 0.4 seed) and 0.22 (:127,385-395,433), and the status line prints both as 'residual'.

title: Default alignment schedule drops py4DSTEM's repeat pass at the smallest bin
evidence: defaultBinSchedule returns [..,2,1] with no repeat at the minimum bin (ParallaxAlignment.swift:153-166), while py4DSTEM defaults num_iter_at_min_bin=2 and appends a repeat (parallax.py:1141,1276-1281). This is already tracked as Gate D diagnosed 2026-09-17, fix owed (docs/open-items.md:105-114), with the reference.py trap noted.

title: Alignment working-memory guard counts three stacks; six are live
evidence: The guard prices 3 x stackByteCount plus FFT work (ParallaxAlignment.swift:308-316). With `previous` set, normalizedStack, previous.shiftedStack, previous.shiftedMasks, the new shiftedStack and shiftedMasks (:403-406) and a rollPlanes copy (:441-452) are live at once, and preprocessing also keeps unshiftedStack (ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:166-168). Peak memory can be about 2x the 1 GiB it admits; the numbers are unaffected.

title: Parallax and ptychography use the raw aperture centre as the diffraction origin, bypassing `Calibration.referenceOrigin` — the one derivation the type says every caller must use
evidence: Structurally true: ParallaxPhysicalCalibration.resolve takes the aperture centre as origin (ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:95-99), not Calibration.referenceOrigin (Calibration.swift:738-763). In practice they usually coincide: origin calibration, file load and restore recentre the aperture on the mean origin (AppState+Calibration.swift:113-117, AppState+Open.swift:484-510,1043-1046), and a user aperture move clears the maps/recorded mean and sets .manual (AppState+Open.swift:1056-1084). They diverge only when the aperture is set without updateAperture, e.g. a replayed virtual-detector step (AppState+Replay.swift:151).

title: Parallax and ptychography refuse to run without an R–Q rotation calibration that neither pipeline ever reads
evidence: resolve() refuses without a finite rotation (ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:58-62). Ptychography now reads it: D002, fixed 2026-09-09, rotates and transposes scan positions (PtychographyPreparation.swift:115-200). Parallax still never reads physical.rotationRad/transpose (its aberration fit recovers or forces its own rotation, ParallaxAberrationFitting.swift:158-201), so the parallax half stands; it is the repeat of core-analysis-physics-02/D005.

title: `StrainMapping.compute` scores a manual basis over a different observation population than an automatic one (`minRadius: 0` vs the default 2), so the exported `basis_support_fraction` means two different things
evidence: A manual basis is scored over vectorObservations(minRadius: 0) (StrainMapping.swift:168-171), which includes the central beam, while the automatic path uses the default minRadius 2 (:338,369). scoreBasis never counts (0,0) as support (:580), so the manual basis_support_fraction (:290, exported at ResultExport.swift:1394) has the central-beam count in its denominator and reads lower by roughly one peak per pattern.

title: `MetalEngine`'s six compute pipelines are unsynchronized `lazy var`s on a nonisolated process-wide singleton
evidence: MetalEngine is a `nonisolated final class` singleton (MetalEngine.swift:118-120) documented for use from Task.detached (:7-10), with six `private(set) lazy var` PSOs (:140-157) and no lock; Swift 5 mode does not diagnose it. Two background tasks first-using the same pipeline at once would race the lazy init (double build or a torn store). The window is first use only.

title: The azimuthal blur width is a plan-generation parameter but a hard-coded literal in the matcher, so template and experimental images can be built with different kernels
evidence: OrientationPlan.generate takes azimBlurBins (OrientationPlan.swift:107,141) but does not store it (the plan keeps intensityPower and radialKernelInvAngstrom only, :82-86,350), and the matcher hard-codes azimBlurBins: 1.5 (OrientationMatcher.swift:238,306). The only production caller uses the default (AppState+ACOM.swift:165-169), so there is no mismatch today; it is latent.

title: Polar deposition converts a radius to an Int bin index with no finiteness or magnitude guard — a runtime trap on a bad Q calibration
evidence: buildPolar does Int(exact.rounded()) and Int(a/2pi*n) with no finiteness or magnitude guard (OrientationPlan.swift:257-262), so a NaN or huge r traps. A 'bad Q calibration' cannot reach it as NaN/Inf/negative, because reciprocalInvAngstromPerPixel rejects those (Calibration.swift:145) and the exploratory slider is clamped to 0.001...0.05 (MapSettings.swift:1129-1134). A trap needs an absurd finite Q (~1e14 per px) or a non-finite peak/origin.

title: writeCalibration silently discards per-position origin maps that fail its validity test, while the export path refuses on the same condition
evidence: writeCalibration does drop maps silently (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1715-1723), but its test is internal consistency (2-D shape, counts), not the export refusal's frame match against the view (:1161-1167), so the two are not the 'same condition'. For app-built snapshots the writeCalibration drop is unreachable, because ResultExport.swift:1310-1321 always builds consistent maps; the silent drop that can happen is upstream, where that snapshot omits off-frame maps without a word.

title: Re-referencing wipes `originProvenance` to `.geometricDefault` while a valid recorded mean origin survives and silently becomes the reference origin
evidence: When re-referencing drops the origin maps (scan-shape mismatch :176-183, or a fitted origin outside the detector crop :206-213), it sets originProvenance = .geometricDefault. The recorded mean is moved and kept when inside (:268-276), and a file with qx0_mean plus maps sets both (AppState+Open.swift:483-511). Calibration.referenceOrigin then returns .recordedMean (Calibration.swift:752-757) while the provenance reads 'Geometric default (unfitted)', and parallax refuses on that label (ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:49).

title: The demo fixture is square on every axis and declares a symmetric origin, so nothing built on it can catch a scan- or detector-axis transposition
evidence: True that the shape is square on both axis pairs ([12,12,64,64], DemoFourDDataSource.swift:9) and the declared origin is symmetric (qx0Mean=qy0Mean=32, constant maps, :94-106); closed-items-2026-09.md:537-543 records D002's transpose result being a geometric no-op on this cube. But the pattern CONTENT is not symmetric under either transposition (probe offset -phase in x vs +0.6*phase in y with phase=scanX-scanY, texture sin(7x+11y+13scanX+17scanY), :115-141), so a content-level assertion on it can catch a swap; only shape/origin-based checks cannot.

title: Synthetic demo calibration is stamped .importedFile, so fabricated numbers are labelled as read from a file
evidence: The demo's synthetic PixelCalibration (DemoFourDDataSource.swift:91-107) goes through the generic file path, which stamps rScale/qScale/rotation/probe provenance .importedFile (AppState+Open.swift:462-477) and originProvenance .fileMaps (:510); openDemoFixture (:128-132) has no override. Reached from the welcome screen's Try Demo Data, so readiness rows read "From file" for fabricated values. Cosmetic: the whole dataset is a labelled fixture.

title: The whole resident-cube path in FourDArray/ResidentCube is unreachable in the shipping app — no caller ever requests .resident
evidence: Nothing in the app requests .resident: DatasetResidency.mode defaults to .streamed and request(_:) has no caller in App/UI/Session; preloadResidentCube (AppState+Open.swift:700-712) says so itself, and docs/open-items.md:314-318 records 'nothing does today'. It is a deliberate, documented state (the .automatic path was dropped by decision), reachable only from tools/tests, not an accidental dead path.

title: The diffraction-pattern LRU is bounded by pattern COUNT, not bytes, and nothing in the app ever clears it
evidence: True: the LRU is 96 patterns by count (FourDArray.swift:32-34, 414-420), so its byte cost scales with qy*qx (~400 MB at 1024x1024 float32), and clearCache() (:82) has no caller. Overstated: the cache is an instance field of the per-dataset FourDArray and is freed when activate replaces the array, so it does not grow across datasets.

title: H5Reader.readProbe materialises the entire probe dataset from file-declared dims, then discards all but slice 0
evidence: readProbe allocates and reads count = dims.reduce(1,*) floats (H5Reader.swift:499-509) where the slice-count axis (dims[0] when slicesFirst, dims[2] otherwise) is unchecked (:488-491), then keeps only slice 0 (:511-516). A probe stack with many slices is read whole; the unchecked product can also overflow-trap on a crafted file. A hyperslab read of slice 0 would avoid both.

title: Rehydrated upsample_factor from a sidecar has no upper bound and reaches an Int(Double) conversion that traps
evidence: parse accepts any finite upsample_factor >= 1 (ResultPresentation.swift:195, 262-265). applySelectedSavedControls copies it into parallaxKDEUpsampleFactor (Support/ResultExport.swift:932), and the reconstructor computes Int((Double(stackHeight)*factor).rounded()) (ParallaxSubpixelReconstruction.swift:165-170) before its overflow guard, which traps when the product exceeds Int.max. Concrete input: a sidecar with upsample_factor "1e300", then apply saved controls and run KDE. The UI NumericField (UI/PhaseSettings.swift:396-399) is also unbounded, so a typed value hits the same trap.

title: EMPAD and MIB whole-cube reads open, seek, read and close a fresh FileHandle for every single diffraction pattern
evidence: EMPADReader.read opens a FileHandle, seeks, reads and closes on every call (VendorRawReaders.swift:209-217). readPattern calls it once per frame (:92, and MIB :313), and readScanRow/readScanTile loop readPattern (:116-146, :333-361), so a whole-cube pass does one open/close per diffraction pattern. This is a performance cost; no result changes.

title: `to_counts` is applied to the cropped window in Swift and to the whole native pattern in Python — an unmarked deviation that gives each >256-px window its own dose scale
evidence: Swift calls modelInputs on each cropped window (LearnedDiskDetector.swift:414), which applies toCounts to that window's own max (:130-135, 144). Python applies to_counts to the whole native pattern before fit_to (tools/disk-detector/evaluate.py:48-50). For a float cube with max<=1 on a detector >256 px, each window is scaled by its own max and log1p compresses differently, so candidate picks can differ. Detectors <=256 px pad and keep the same max. There is no DEVIATION note.

title: Strain staleness ignores the manual g-vector basis, which is an input to the computation
evidence: The strain staleness signature holds only reference_mode and basis_mode (StrainProduct.swift:120-125, used via ProductWorkflow.swift:463 and compared in stalenessVerdict :390-402). The manual g1X/g1Y/g2X/g2Y fields feed manualInitialBasis (:111-113) but are not in the signature. Input: set the basis to Manual, run strain, then edit g1: the map still reads current. The selected reference region is not in the signature either.

title: The GPU threadgroup argmax and the CPU argmax break ties in different directions, contradicting the shader's own "identical to the reference path" claim
evidence: True that the tie rules differ. The CPU keeps the first (lowest) bin (OrientationMatcher.swift:203). The GPU tree reduction with strict '>' (ACOMMatching.metal:77-83) returns an order-dependent bin: with 128 bins tied at 32 and 64 it returns 64. Overstated: the comment's 'identical' claim is about TEMPLATE selection, which both paths do in the shared CPU selectOrientation (OrientationMatcher.swift:509-513). The two paths also compute scores with different arithmetic (direct DFT vs FFT), so exact float ties are rare and are usually symmetry-equivalent bins.

title: The app's CoM component order is transposed relative to py4DSTEM, so the R–Q rotation it reports and exports is the negative of py4DSTEM's — and of its own parallax-fitted rotation
evidence: The app transliterates py4DSTEM's rotation/curl formulas with x = column (RotationCalibration.swift:138-164; CenterOfMass.metal:49-64) while reading axes as (Ry,Rx,Qy,Qx) (DatasetDescriptor.swift:39-42), which negates the angle. This is now a tracked open item, 'App R-Q rotation is -py4DSTEM's ... QR_rotation crosses the boundary unconverted' (docs/open-items.md:24-38, reopened 2026-09-23), measured +80.0 vs -80.1 deg on a real file. QR_rotation is imported (AppState+Open.swift:469) and exported (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1690-1697) unconverted. Not a repeat of core-analysis-physics-06. The parallax-rotation part of the claim is not verified here.

title: The main-thread regression guard exists only for the learned detector; the classical full-scan path — the shipped default and the one that actually froze the app — has none, and the build cannot catch a lost `nonisolated`
evidence: True that the only main-thread guard is the learned test (LearnedDiskDetectionScanTests.swift:282-318) and no test checks the classical TiledDiskDetection.detectAll (declared nonisolated at TiledDiskDetection.swift:72) off the main actor. Wrong that the classical path 'actually froze the app': the repo's own record puts the 847/847 main-thread freeze in the learned detectAll (LearnedDiskDetection.swift:206-215).

title: The learned parity gate skips rather than fails on any Core ML load error, and falls back to the repo copy of the asset so a bundle-packaging regression is invisible
evidence: loadDetector turns any Core ML load error into XCTSkip (LearnedDiskDetectorTests.swift:115-118). assetURL falls back to the repo copy when the bundle has none (:25-28), so an app bundle missing the .mlpackage still runs every parity test green. No test or inventory check asserts that bundledAssetURL() is non-nil in the test host. Skips do appear in the xcodebuild skipped count.

title: Every learned-detector parity test silently XCTSkips when the asset cannot load, because the guard tests only that the .mlpackage DIRECTORY exists
evidence: Duplicate of D104's mechanism: the directory-existence guard (:116) plus the catch-all skip (:118) do make the parity tests skip on a load failure. But testCommittedAssetHashMatchesItsRecordAndTheFixture (:210-216) FAILS rather than skips when the package contents differ from the recorded hash, so the D001 case (a missing model spec inside an existing directory) is caught. Not every such failure is silent.

title: The frozen hand-labelled test set that is the sole evidence for the shipped 0.7 threshold exists only in a `/private/tmp` worktree
evidence: The labels directory is gitignored (.gitignore:44) and no labels file is in the repo. overnight-256.sh:22,56-60 runs without it when absent. The only recorded location is a /private/tmp scratchpad worktree (docs/archive/v3/learned-detector-2026-09-06.md:600). ADR 014 and Models/DiskDetector/disk-detector-heatmap-256.json:19 cite this set as the threshold evidence. Whether the file still exists on the owner's disk cannot be checked from the repo, but the evidence for the shipped 0.7 cannot be reproduced from the public repo.

title: The py4DSTEM source lock is verified by HEAD only — a dirty or de-gitted `References/py4DSTEM-dev` is accepted as "lock present"
evidence: fetch-py4dstem.sh:17-27 compares only HEAD to the lock when .git exists. It never runs git status or diff, so a dirty tree at the lock commit prints 'lock present'. Without .git it checks nothing but the presence of version.py. Only individual harnesses such as rotation-parity-test's assert_source_contract check source content.

title: `fetch-py4dstem.sh` verifies nothing once the checkout exists: no content check without `.git`, and no check at all when HEAD already equals the lock
evidence: Same code as D107 (fetch-py4dstem.sh:17-28): when HEAD equals the lock nothing is verified, and without .git there is no content check. Only the fresh-clone path checks version.py (:34). This is a duplicate of D107.

title: Merging ml/disk-detector today red-lines main's own inventory gate, and taking the branch's tools/run-tests.sh would silently delete three of its checks
evidence: The ml/disk-detector branch no longer exists (git branch -a lists only main, the current cloud branch and one claude/ branch). docs/archive/git-cleanup-2026-09-17.md:70 audited it as fully re-landed, superseded or retired, and the main-only directive rules out a merge.

title: The C5 AppState/ResultExport growth gate is blind whenever HEAD is a docs-only commit, which is this repo's normal closeout shape
evidence: On a clean tree the C5 measurement compares HEAD with HEAD^ (run-tests.sh:192, 202-206). If HEAD is a docs-only commit, both hold the same AppState/ResultExport, so growth from the previous commit reads 0, and pre-push judges only the tip. Impact is reduced: since 2026-09-16 C5 only reports and no longer fails (:208-215).

title: `LearnedDiskDetector.heatmaps` reads the Core ML output as densely packed and never checks its strides or channel count
evidence: heatmaps checks rank 4, batch and the two spatial dims (LearnedDiskDetector.swift:288-291) but not shape[1] (channels) or array.strides, then copies the first batch*S*S elements as if dense (:293-304). This is latent: with the shipped single-channel fp16 256x256 output the rows are 512 B and dense, and the fixture parity test would catch a mismatch.

title: The shaders are compiled with -fmetal-math-mode=fast, which voids the NaN reasoning written into OriginMeasure.metal and the NaN robustness OriginCalibration claims for the statistics it consumes
evidence: True that the shaders build with MTL_FAST_MATH = YES in both configurations (project.pbxproj:421, 486), so IEEE NaN semantics are not guaranteed. Overstated: no shader has an isnan or isfinite check to be optimised away. OriginMeasure.metal:44-50 already concedes garbage on an all-NaN pattern, and OriginCalibration's isFinite filters (OriginCalibration.swift:132-178) run on the CPU, which fast math does not affect. Whether partially-NaN input yields finite garbage on the GPU needs a run.

title: ActivityLog's two drop rules are textual heuristics that can silently discard a real event
evidence: record drops any message ending in '%' (ActivityLog.swift:81) and any message the previous stored line ends with (:82, hasSuffix, not equality), so a shorter distinct event that happens to be a suffix of the last line is lost. No current status string ending in '%' was found, so no concrete loss was shown.

title: `AppState.sessionInventory` carries an orphaned doc comment describing a property that was deleted, contradicting the comment directly below it
evidence: AppState.swift:392-393 carry an orphaned comment ('Set only while resultPresentation.resultImage is the scalar map restored ... New scientific results clear it') directly above the real doc line for sessionInventory (:394-395), which describes something else.

title: productWorkflowReadiness probes the app bundle on the filesystem every time a view body reads it
evidence: True that every read of productWorkflowReadiness (AppState.swift:953-970, read from about 9 view sites) calls LearnedDiskDetector.bundledAssetURL(), a Bundle.url(forResource:) lookup (Core/ML/LearnedDiskDetection.swift:316-318). Whether that reaches the filesystem each time is unproven, since Bundle caches resource lookups; there is no measured cost.

title: `publishRestoredProduct` is the one publish site that does not bump `resultVersion`, and every display cache is keyed on it
evidence: publishRestoredProduct itself calls replaceProduct without a bump (AppState.swift:345-358), but all four call sites bump right after: Support/ResultExport.swift:803/813 then :825, and AppState+Open.swift:979/989 then :996. Every display cache keyed on resultVersion is invalidated. At most a latent footgun for a future caller.

title: `applyDPCDisplay` returns nil for two different facts — "the display was published" and "this did not run"
evidence: The guard at AppState+DPC.swift:119 returns nil ('did not run') when there is no comField, no descriptor or the mode is not .dpc, which is the same value as success at :178. In runDPC (:59-62), if the user leaves the DPC mode before the field lands, the run still writes 'DPC ✓', records a recipe step and returns published with nothing published. The calibration callers (:101, AppState+Calibration.swift:268) are unaffected.

title: Colormaps.lutRGBA traps (not returns garbage) for count <= 1
evidence: count=1 gives t=0/0=NaN, and sample() then fails every comparison and returns (1,1,1) (Colormaps.swift:26-55), so it yields white with no trap. count=0 returns an empty array. Only a negative count traps (array allocation, :12), and every caller passes a constant 44, 128 or 256.

title: PendingLoad owns a security-scoped URL and a live read Task but has no deinit; release depends entirely on two AppState call sites
evidence: PendingLoad holds url/accessedSecurityScope and singleDPFetch (PendingLoad.swift:80-84, 180) and has no deinit. The scope is released only at AppState+Open.swift:66-71 (displaced by replace) and AppState+Promote.swift:167-176 (discard); commit hands it to openURL (:31-32). A pending load alive when its AppState goes away (window closed with the configurator open) keeps the scope until process exit.

title: Quantitative iDPC forces a square scan step even when the two scan axes are sampled differently
evidence: Literally true: physicalIDPCCalibration sets row and column sampling from the one realPixelSize (DPC.swift:123-127). But the calibration model has only one R scale (Calibration.swift:564, and DM4Reader.swift:766 reads one axis). py4DSTEM does the same, _scan_sampling = (R_pixel_size,)*2 (phase_base_class.py:515), so this is parity, not a port defect, and there is no source of an anisotropic step to honour.

title: The sampled-preview label the file's own invariant I4 calls load-bearing prints "every 32th position"
evidence: ordinal() special-cases only 1, 2 and 3 (DatasetPreview.swift:74-81), so strides 21, 22, 23 and 32 print '21th', '22th', '23th', '32th'. stride() can return any integer (:124). The summary is the I4 label (:55-64).

title: DatasetPreview.make reports two non-allocation failures as FourDError.allocationFailed
evidence: make throws FourDError.allocationFailed for a non-4D or empty descriptor (DatasetPreview.swift:152-154) and for a pattern-size mismatch (:168-170), neither of which is an allocation. The user text 'Could not allocate or read the requested 4D-STEM tile' (FourDArray.swift:9-10) half-fits the second and misleads on the first.

title: Full-scan progress fractions can be delivered out of order, and the tile coalescer admits the regression
evidence: DiskDetection.swift:1172-1180 decides the tick under rowsDone but calls progress(f) after unlock, so a worker holding f=k/N can deliver after another worker delivered (k+1)/N. TiledDiskDetection.swift:13-23 ProgressCoalescer admits any bucket != lastBucket, so a lower (older) bucket passes too. Effect is a progress bar that can briefly step backwards; no result is affected.

title: fit2D and fitOrigin(included:) index by width*height without checking the array actually has that many elements
evidence: fit2D (OriginCalibration.swift:443-500) indexes z[ry*width+rx] and included[...] and fitOrigin(included:) (:219-238) indexes included[$0] with no count check; fitOriginTrimmed (:340) checks only measuredY.count == measuredX.count. A mismatched array traps on the bounds check rather than corrupting anything, and every in-app caller (tiledRun :600-613, run :757-770) builds arrays of exactly d.ry*d.rx, so it is a latent precondition.

title: OriginCalibration.run is dead in the app and duplicates tiledRun's calibration logic
evidence: OriginCalibration.swift:726-733 says itself that run(cube:) has no callers; grep finds only mac4DSTEMTests/ProbeSizeTests.swift:84,210,275. It repeats tiledRun's mean-DP -> probeSize -> measure -> fitOriginTrimmed sequence (:735-783 vs :543-625) and has no originMethod/.friedel option. The code comment already names deleting it as an owner option.

title: Q high-pass envelope is applied although py4DSTEM's aberration_correct ignores it
evidence: ParallaxAberrationCorrection.swift:170-175 multiplies in a Butterworth high-pass whenever qHighpassInvAngstrom is set, and the user can set it (AppState+PhaseContrast.swift:495). At the pinned reference, parallax.py:2809-2893 accepts q_highpass but applies only q_lowpass. The extension is opt-in and noted at :14-15 but has no DEVIATION tag, and the parity fixture tools/parallax-aberration-test/reference.py:259-260 reimplements the high-pass itself, so this case is checked against the app's own formula, not py4DSTEM.

title: ProbeKernel.measured traps on a non-finite origin where its sibling .flat returns nil
evidence: In the sigmoid-trench path, ProbeKernel.swift:179-180 does Int(floor(-originY/X)), which traps on NaN, infinity or out-of-Int-range values, while flat() guards originX/Y.isFinite at :256-258. The callers pass calibration.referenceOrigin (AppState+DiskDetection.swift:67-72) or probeSize (:113-116), so a trap needs a non-finite mean origin.

title: RotationCalibration.solve reads 2*width*height floats from com without checking its length
evidence: RotationCalibration.swift:181-187 reads com[2*i] and com[2*i+1] for i < width*height and never checks com.count, so a short array traps. The only caller (AppState+Calibration.swift:236-244) builds com and the dimensions from the same descriptor, so it is latent.

title: Analytic aperture kernel and the mask path disagree on the exact-centre detector pixel when inner radius is 0
evidence: The analytic kernel (VirtualAperture.metal:52, strict r2 > rIn2) is used only for the .annulus shape (AppState+ResultPresentation.swift:258-262 -> VirtualDetector.tiledRun -> run :532-542). The mask path for .annulus uses the same strict test (VirtualDetector.swift:583-585, includeInnerBoundary false), so the two agree on the centre pixel at inner=0. The only difference is .circle (inclusive, :580-582) versus annulus-with-inner-0, which follows py4DSTEM make_detector (virtualimage.py:635 circle vs :649-651 annulus); the BF preset maps to .circle (AppState+ResultPresentation.swift:169).

title: Blocking whole-cube compute and the on-screen MTKView renders share one MTLCommandQueue, so a long dispatch serialises ahead of the display command buffers
evidence: The code does share one queue: MetalEngine.swift:167/175 creates the only MTLCommandQueue, compute run() commits on it and waitUntilCompleted (:362-374), and MetalImageView.swift:227 draws on the same queue. Whether a long whole-cube dispatch actually delays display frames enough to see is not established from source; an Instruments/Metal System Trace capture on a large resident cube would settle it.

title: The CIF importer's family-classification tolerance is 1000× looser than the model validation it feeds, so a band of cells is rejected with a generic message that hides the real reason
evidence: classifyFamily (CIFImport.swift:816-821) uses 1e-3 relative on lengths and 0.05 deg absolute on angles, but CrystalModel.validationIssues (CrystalModel.swift:103-118) uses 1e-6 relative. Example: a=4.000, b=4.002, c=4.000, 90/90/90 is classified .cubic, fails cubic_symmetry_mismatch, and is rejected at CIFImport.swift:146-148, while a=4.000, b=4.006 loads as .identity. The error names the a=b=c requirement but not that the importer chose cubic. MaterialsProjectImport reuses the same classifier.

title: A singular metric tensor silently yields latInv = latReal — a reciprocal lattice in Å instead of Å⁻¹, with no error
evidence: Crystal.swift:113-115 falls back with invert3x3(metric) ?? identity3, and invert3x3 returns nil when |det| <= 1e-15 (:379-380), so latInv = latReal with no error. det(metric) = V^2, so this needs 0 < V < ~3e-8 A^3; V = 0 or NaN is already refused by CrystalModel.swift:58-59. No physical cell reaches it, but the fallback is silent.

title: Restoring an RGBA result map computes width*height*4 after a guard that only bounds width*height
evidence: readResultShape (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1018) guards only width <= Int.max/height, and readRGBAResultMap then allocates width*height*4 (:967), which overflow-traps when width*height > Int.max/4. D141 covers this in practice: any huge declared extent traps on allocation first. It needs a damaged or crafted sidecar.

title: Preserved results are re-keyed by kind, so two saved results whose kind attribute is missing collapse into one and the second is dropped without a word
evidence: readResultDescriptor defaults a missing mac4dstem_kind to "unknown" (:839-840). The preservation loop (:1573-1588) renames each node to resultNodeName(forKind:) and `guard copiedNodeNames.insert(targetName).inserted else { continue }` drops the second node of the same kind. Its id is also in the reserved set (:1550-1552), so the external-object copy skips it too, and it is lost with no message. The app always writes the kind (:1790, :1878), so this needs a foreign or damaged sidecar.

title: An orphaned result_* node is copied as an opaque 'external object' and then collides with a new result of the same kind, wedging every future save
evidence: Confirmed: a root child that is not a readable manifest result (not listed, or readResultDescriptor returns nil at :687-691) is copied as an opaque external object (:1544-1566). A later save of the same kind then calls createGroup on the same name (:1786/:1874, :2049-2056), which fails and throws; the atomic publish keeps the old file, and the orphan survives into every rewrite. Overstated: only saves that write that same kind fail; other results and calibration saves succeed. It also needs a file this writer did not produce.

title: Result and calibration array sizes are taken from the file with no upper bound, so a damaged sidecar traps on allocation instead of erroring
evidence: readResultShape (:1014-1019) and readDoubleMatrix (:814-817) bound extents only by Int.max products, then allocate from the file-declared size (:913, :967, :817) with no cap and no check against the loaded scan. An HDF5 dataspace can declare enormous dims with unallocated chunked storage, so a damaged sidecar traps on allocation in loadInventory or restore instead of throwing.

title: `originFitIsSane` passes vacuously when no probe radius is set, and the reciprocal-metrology gate does not require one
evidence: originFitIsSane (Calibration.swift:651-654) returns true when rmsResidual or probeRadius is nil, and originSupportsReciprocalMetrology (:686-693) adds only the origin-kind check. Reachable input: a py4DSTEM file with origin maps but no probe_semiangle (AppState+Open.swift:469, 502-507) gives kind .fittedMaps, so the gate passes with no residual judged. File maps without measured arrays also make rmsResidual nil (:487-491).

title: `CalibrationInvalidation.Field.probeRadius` and `.ellipse` are never produced, so two session-restore guards can never fire
evidence: The only producers are CalibrationReReference.swift:181,214,241,282 (.origin), :334 (.scanIndexedResults) and AppState+Open.swift:880 (.sessionCalibration). .probeRadius and .ellipse (:63-64) are never constructed, so the guards at AppState+Open.swift:926-927 and :934-935 always pass. This matches the note at CalibrationReReference.swift:289-298 that a crop leaves radius and ellipse unchanged, so the guards are dead code, not a missed invalidation.

title: DM4Error.unsupportedDataType is never thrown; an unsupported pixel type is reported to the user as "no datacube found"
evidence: DM4Error.unsupportedDataType is defined (DM4Reader.swift:20,28) and never thrown. locateDatacube skips any array whose DataType has pixelSize 0 (:581-582; e.g. complex 3/13 or RGB 23) with `continue` and ends at :663 with throw DM4Error.noDatacube, so a 4D cube of an unsupported type is reported as "No 4D ... datacube was found".

title: FourDArray.scanTile validates only the tile's element count and row range, not its declared scan/detector extents
evidence: FourDArray.scanTile (FourDArray.swift:87-114) checks only yRange and pixels.count, not tile.scanWidth, detectorHeight or detectorWidth. Most consumers index by the descriptor, but the Friedel path (OriginCalibration.swift:662-676) strides a raw pointer by tile.scanWidth, so a reader returning wrong extents with the right count would over-read. ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:485-487 checks the extents itself. Latent, since every reader is in-repo.

title: H5 EMD dim-vector calibration infers pixel size from the first two samples only, with no uniformity check and a silent drop for descending axes
evidence: H5Reader.swift:852-859 takes pixel size as v[1]-v[0] from the dim vector. It does not check uniformity or that the vector length matches the axis, requires v[1]-v[0] > 0 (a descending axis returns nil, silently leaving no calibration), and drops vectors over 65536 entries.

title: A sidecar with no recorded ptychography method is rehydrated as gradient-descent and reported as an applied setting
evidence: Confirmed: ResultPresentation.swift:218-220 maps a missing method to "gradient-descent", and :173 lists it as an applied setting. But the current writer always records method (Support/ResultExport.swift:1529), so nil comes only from sidecars written before the key existed, or edited by hand. If those builds were GD-only, the inference is correct. The truncated local git history cannot settle when the key was added.

title: cancelCurrent() cannot distinguish "already cancelling" from "nothing was running", and the controller keeps reporting a live operation after cancel
evidence: The API facts are true: cancelCurrent (:60-64) returns nil both when nothing is running and when the op is already cancelled, and active stays set until finish(token) (:48-52). But the only caller (AppState.swift:1105-1108) uses nil just to skip rewriting "Cancelling ..." status, which is right in both cases. Keeping the op live until the worker unwinds is accurate, because the work is still running. No user-visible defect.

title: `LearnedDetectionSession.prepare` has a check-then-await gap that can load and compile the Core ML model twice
evidence: LearnedDetectionSession is @MainActor, and prepare (LearnedDetection.swift:134-148) checks `detector` and then awaits LearnedDiskDetector.load. Reentrant callers (livePeaks :181-184 on pattern changes, prepareForRun :163-171) can both see nil and both load and compile, and the first to finish resets `preparing` while the second is still loading. The cost is a duplicate load; both detectors are equivalent.

title: A session with no recorded origin makes `apply` invent an aperture centre in the wrong frame and can emit a false "beam is not inside this diffraction crop" refusal
evidence: With no saved origin, SessionCalibrationFramePolicy.swift:117-127 passes the loaded view's centre (view.descriptor.qx/2, qy/2) as a source-frame apertureCenter. CalibrationReReference.swift:228-245 then subtracts the crop offset and bins it. Example: a full-extent session reopened with a detector crop at x offset 100, width 100 gives x=50-100=-50, which is outside, so a false .origin invalidation ("direct beam is not inside this diffraction crop") is appended and shown (AppState+Open.swift:903-905). The moved centre itself is discarded (:130), so no number changes.

title: The Bragg-peak CSV export carries no units, no calibration and no frame, so a CSV from a cropped or binned view is indistinguishable from a full-extent one
evidence: The Bragg-peak CSV export no longer exists at HEAD: grep -i csv over mac4DSTEM/ and mac4DSTEMTests/ finds only the header comment at ResultExport.swift:5. docs/architecture.md:105,144 still describe a CSV export, which is stale. The claim was a repeat of support-export-08 (docs/archive/2026-08-31-review/README.md:80, "narrowed").

title: Region-radius Slider forms an inverted range on a scan whose larger axis is a single pixel
evidence: ImagingSettings.swift:101 uses `in: 1...Double(max(d.rx, d.ry) / 2)`. Integer division gives 0 when max(rx,ry)==1, and `1...0` fails the ClosedRange precondition (a trap) as soon as the Radius row renders (non-point region shape, :94). Input: a [1,1,qy,qx] HDF5 cube (rank 4 is accepted, H5Reader.swift:546) or a crop to one scan pixel, then picking a circle or rectangle region. Other sliders guard with max(1, ...) (MapSettings.swift:512, ExportSheet.swift:167).

title: A full-pattern log10 transform runs on the main thread inside a SwiftUI view body, for a histogram that is inside a DisclosureGroup collapsed by default
evidence: The inspector DisclosureGroup is gone: WorkspaceInspector.swift:490-498 records the histogram moving into the pane popover. The full-pattern log10 (DiffractionPattern.contrastPixels, DiffractionPattern.swift:85-89) still runs in a view body on the main actor at PaneOverlays.swift:326-327. It now runs only while the diffraction popover that shows the histogram is open, but again on every body re-evaluation, for example while dragging a range handle.

title: TB1StallProbeTests is inert everywhere: every test in the file skips on a hard-coded absolute path inside the owner's home directory
evidence: The two TB1StallProbeTests cases skip via requireFile on the owner's absolute path (TB1StallProbeTests.swift:18-27), so they do nothing on any other machine or in CI. "Every test ... inert everywhere" is wrong: docs/status.md:16 (2026-09-23 run, 869 tests) reports one skip total on the owner's machine, and the file's BookmarkResolutionLatencyTests (:104-150) skip on recents state, not on the path.

title: `tools/lib/python.sh`'s last-resort fallback accepts a `python3` with numpy but no scipy, contradicting the candidate loop it comments
evidence: The candidate loop (tools/lib/python.sh:14-15) requires `import numpy, scipy`, but the last-resort fallback (:21-26) accepts any python3 with numpy alone. A harness that imports scipy would then fail with a visible ImportError, not silently.
